- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4499 (`security_pass_successor_local_id="security-pass-fix-cycle-$((security_pass_successor_cycles + 1))"`) and scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4517-4518 (the `--arg local_id_marker "- Local ID: \`${security_pass_successor_local_id}\`"`) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The marker contract used by `resolve_security_pass_fix_successor` is a private, exact-substring handshake with the body produced by `create_security_pass_fix_issue` (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4624-4631) and the verbatim-copy path in `close_and_reissue` at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:11064-11077. If any future refactor reorders the orchestrator-metadata block, drops the leading `- `, or changes the backtick delimiter in either side, every successor adoption silently fails closed (the helper returns 1) and the project terminalises as `ai:security-pass-failed` even when a live successor exists.
  WHY: `jq -sr ... index($local_id_marker)` requires the entire literal string (including backticks, spaces, and the leading `- `) to appear on a single body line. The dependency is documented only in prose, not pinned in code, so the two call sites can drift.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4520-4522 (the `if length == 0 or (all(.[]; type == "array") | not) then error(...)` guard inside `resolve_security_pass_fix_successor`) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When the GitHub API legitimately returns zero managed issues (`[]`), the helper exits jq with an error and the surrounding function returns 2 (inconclusive) rather than 1 (no successor).
  WHY: A repo with no other `ai:orchestrator-managed` issues open at the moment of the poll tick will have its predecessor treated as inconclusive; every tick re-issues the same warn line and never falls through to `security_pass_closed_fix_failure`. The pre-existing `create_security_pass_fix_issue` block at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4654-4658 has the same shape, so this is an inherited pattern, but the new helper is the first one to gate terminalisation on the empty-page case.
